text:
pagerbot: INCIDENT PAGE — autoscaler failed to obtain GPUs in gcp-west1; quota denied during scale-up. Pager triggered for oncall @emily.g. Incident severity: P1. Link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/1768765432 :rotating_light:

emily.g: on it. seeing a big backlog on the inference queue (embed & chat).

emily.g: quick numbers from the dashboard: pending queue ~11.7k requests, 95p latency 2.1s, error rate 17.9% last 10m.

raj.patel: confirming autoscaler logs show repeated quota error from GCP: `quotaExceeded` on resource `NVIDIA_T4` region `us-west1` when trying to create instance group.

maria_k: grabbing more logs. looks like allocator tried three scale-up waves and each got denied. stack snippet:
```
I0321 14:02:11 autoscaler.go:345] scaling up: requested 8 x n1-standard-8 + 4 x nvidia-t4, response: quotaExceeded: Requested GPU cores > available quota
I0321 14:04:22 autoscaler.go:413] retrying; backlog still growing
```

kevin_t: any preemptible/spot nodes involved? if preemptible failed we should fallback to on-demand pools.

emily.g: no, these are regular reserved pools. quota hit on region-level GPU count not preemption.

raj.patel: immediate mitigation plan I propose: 1) throttle incoming routing to reduce queue growth (admit-control), 2) route non-critical workloads to gcp-us-west2, 3) enable model-fallback to quantized model-small for new sessions, 4) open quota escalation with GCP support and request emergency increase.

maria_k: running admit-control patch now. lowering concurrency + reject low-priority jobs. patch command:
```
# temporarily reduce max_concurrency for /v1/generate
kubectl patch configmap routing-config -n runtime --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_concurrency":"6"}}'
```

emily.g: admit-control applied. traffic drop expected ~35%. watching queue.

support_sam: starting customer triage: checking which customers are impacted. preliminary: two enterprise customers in us-west1 seeing timeouts >10s on streaming. drafting email.

kevin_t: on routing to us-west2: need to ensure model versions exist there and KV cache warming will be slow. suggest redirect only non-streaming batch jobs.

raj.patel: started automated job to reroute batch jobs via feature-flag `region_fallback_v2=true`:
```
# enable fallback for non-interactive routes
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/flags -d '{"flag":"region_fallback_v2","value":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

maria_k: opened GCP quota ticket: https://cloudsupport.google.com/issue/123456789 — requested emergency GPU quota bump + temporary soft quota removal. ETA unknown. added `priority=critical`.

pagerbot: @emily.g oncall handoff scheduled in 18m to @raj.patel per rotation.

emily.g: handoff noted. I'll stay until we confirm routing reduces backlog.

support_sam: customer notification draft (internal):
```
Subject: Degraded inference performance in us-west1
Hi — we're investigating higher-than-normal latencies and timeouts for inference in GCP us-west1. We've activated mitigation steps (traffic throttling and cross-region routing) and will follow up with estimated timelines. No data exposure. Apologies for disruption.
```
Posting to customers in 10m unless situation improves.

raj.patel: metric update: queue dropped from 11.7k -> 6.9k after admit-control + reroute. error rate down to 9.2%. good progress but still above SLO.

kevin_t: lowering per-request batch sizes to reduce required GPU slots per job; updating batching config:
```
PATCH /api/config/batching
{"preferred_batch_size": 8, "max_batch_size": 12}
```

maria_k: also applied a temporary autoscaler patch to ignore GPU-type affinity to allow other GPU models as fallback (e.g., v2->t4 mismatch), but cluster team warned this may increase latency. patch:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata: { name: autoscaler-config, namespace: runtime }
data:
  gpu_fallback_allowed: "true"
EOF
```

emily.g: note: we have a handful of active customers pinned to exact instance types; support is notifying them separately.

support_sam: customer A (finance startup) wants ETA for SLA impact. they are on dedicated capacity in us-west1. opening a direct line.

maria_k: GCP support replied: initial review done, telling us quota is shared across projects; they recommended we close unused GPU claims in region before they can grant more. investigating orphaned pools.

raj.patel: running script to find stale node pools claiming GPUs:
```
gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels:gpu_reserved" --regions=us-west1 --format=json | jq '.[] | {name, status, labels}'
```
Found 3 stale pools (stopped old test clusters) consuming 24 GPUs. sending cleanup job.

kevin_t: cleaning up those pools now. If GCP frees 24 GPUs that'll let one scale-up wave succeed.

emily.g: after cleanup, observed 18 GPUs freed in region per GCP quota API. autoscaler successfully launched 12 GPUs -> new pods came up, queue dropped to 2.4k, errors down to 2.1%.

pagerbot: UPDATE: on-call handoff happening now: @emily.g -> @raj.patel.

emily.g: handing off. actions taken: admit-control, region fallback for batch, batching reduced, GPU pool cleanup, GCP ticket open. Current status: degraded but recovering; monitoring.

raj.patel: taking over. will monitor next hour and coordinate with cloud ops for quota formal increase. will draft RCA skeleton after incident stabilizes.

support_sam: posted customer note to impacted customers. included mitigations and expected follow-ups.

maria_k: follow-ups: 1) set alert when region GPU quota usage >85% of limit (already added), 2) create scheduled job to detect orphaned GPU claims weekly, 3) add cross-region warm caches to reduce cold-start pressure.

kevin_t: plan to add regional capacity buffer policy in autoscaler to avoid reactive scale-ups when region usage >80%. will add config PR.

raj.patel: next update in 15m unless status changes. tagging incident as "mitigated" for active paging, monitoring for 1h.

emily.g: leaving notes in runbook and ops log. thanks team. :thumbsup:
